key_insight: A stage-aware machine-learning model can predict IVF implantation more accurately as later treatment information, especially embryological data, becomes available.
clinical_relevance: This could support more interpretable IVF outcome prediction, while highlighting that embryo-related features are the strongest drivers of model performance.
method: Excluded β-HCG to reduce target leakage.
Trained and compared several models; tuned with stratified cross-validation.
Evaluated a fixed Random Forest model across three IVF stages and interpreted predictions with permutation importance and SHAP.
evidence_signal: The framework was tested on a public IVF dataset with training, validation, and independent test splits, and the final Random Forest performed well on the independent test set.
watch_item: Results need external validation on independent clinical datasets before any clinical use, since performance may not generalize across sites or patient populations.
paper_title: Stage-Aware and Explainable Machine Learning for Predicting IVF Implantation
